rewrite.noticeThis: “In this way” describes how God loved, not merely how much: the cross is the concrete shape of His love, not just a measurement of its volume. Calling Jesus His “one and only” Son marks Him as utterly unique — the irreplaceable gift given for the world.

insight_issue: The insight labels deriving monogenēs from begetting a root-fallacy by asserting it comes from genos rather than gennaō, whereas in Greek morphology -genēs adjectives derive from the root gen- (encompassing both birth and kind); 'unique' is established by semantic usage, not etymological disjunction.

rewrite.noticeThis: The psalmist pairs two closely linked Hebrew words: he praises God for being “wonderfully set apart” (nifleiti), and marvels that God’s works are “wondrous” (nifla'im). Your own life is crafted with the same intentional wonder God displays across creation.

insight_issue: The insight asserts the identical root pala appears twice, but in the Masoretic Text (WLC) nifleiti is from the III-he root pālāh (Strong 6395, 'to distinguish/set apart'), whereas nifla’im is from the III-aleph root pālā’ (Strong 6381, 'to be wonderful').
